clues.title: Coverage: ten small trekkers only
text: Mali has very **limited coverage**. There are only ten small trekkers, divided over seven locations. Instead of learning a lot of country-specific clues, it is more practical to simply memorise what the trekkers look like.
clues.summary: Only ten small trekkers across seven locations. Just memorise what they look like rather than learning country clues.

clues.title: Coverage: tripods, dreamy look
text: All this trekker coverage is made with a regular consumer-grade camera on a **tripod**. This gives all the coverage a very peculiar and recognizable look, which is different from the normal backpack trekkers. It can have a slightly ‘ethereal’ look to it, but it is recommended to simply click on a few of the locations to get a feeling for what it looks like. Objects in the image will usually have motion blur, and slightly saturated colours.
From here on, the Mali tripod trekkers will be simply referred to as “tripods”.
NOTE: Tripods can also be found in several other countries.
clues.summary: All coverage is a normal consumer camera on a tripod, not a backpack. It looks ethereal, with motion blur and slightly saturated colours. Other countries have tripods too.

clues.title: Houses: mud-brick mosques with sticks
text: Almost all the tripods focus on showing **historical mosques**. These tripods usually have an indoor part and an exterior part, which are sometimes not connected to each other.

These mosques have a recognizable look: they are made out of **mud bricks and adobe plaster**. The walls of the buildings are decorated with wooden sticks. Inside, you will usually see the same adobe walls, and prayer rugs on the floor.
clues.summary: Nearly all tripods show old mosques built from mud bricks and adobe plaster, with wooden sticks poking from the walls. Inside are adobe walls and prayer rugs. Most have a separate indoor and outdoor part.

clues.title: Coverage: mosque exteriors look like streets
text: The exterior parts of the mosque tripods can look like a normal street. These will sometimes have [enough information](https://goo.gl/maps/W1WVwXgZUmc7HzhWA) available (when moving) to be included in **pinpointable maps**, like [A Community World](https://www.geoguessr.com/maps/62a44b22040f04bd36e8a914).

This guide has separate sections for the pinpointable and non-pinpointable coverage. You can choose to study only the coverage that is relevant for competitive maps, or all the coverage. Note, however, that the interiors of the mosques are not considered pinpointable, even though they are covered in the section next to their respective exteriors.
clues.summary: Mosque exteriors can look like ordinary streets and are sometimes used in pinpointable maps. The interiors are not pinpointable, even though they sit next to their exteriors.

clues.title: Landscape: dry, sandy and arid
text: Mali is generally an **arid** country. Seeing a sandy, dry landscape can help with immediately distinguishing the Mali tripods from most tripods in other countries.
clues.summary: The country is arid. A sandy, dry landscape helps tell these tripods apart from most tripods elsewhere.

clues.title: Landscape: busy sandy road, trees at mosque
text: The Niono mosque is located in a **busy area** by the side of a wide, sandy and fairly dirty road, with trees right by the walls of the mosque.
It is most easily located on the map by first looking for the “Centre Commercial” slightly north of the centre of Niono.
clues.summary: One mosque stands in a busy area beside a wide, sandy, dirty road, with trees right by its walls. Find it by the Centre Commercial just north of the town centre.

clues.title: Mosque interior: European-style pillars
text: The inside of the Niono mosque can be recognized by its fairly detailed **“European style” pillars**, which is not found in any of the other Malinese mosques with coverage.
clues.summary: The inside has fairly detailed European-style pillars, which none of the other mosques in the country have.

clues.title: Road: sand with bread-slice tiles
text: The roads around the Sidi Yahiya mosque are a mixture of sand and **tiles** shaped like **slices of bread**, which within Mali, is unique to this coverage.

The surrounding buildings are mostly built of bricks having a peachy orange colour with a brown undertone. This can also be found around the other two mosques with coverage in Timbuktu. The area generally looks [busier](https://goo.gl/maps/Pn2Gdp6uaHQPm21Y6) than around the Djingareyber mosque.
clues.summary: Roads are sand mixed with tiles shaped like bread slices, unique in this country. Buildings are peachy-orange brick, as at the other two mosques in the same town. It looks busier than the third mosque.

clues.title: Mosque interior: yellow walls, bare brick base
text: The interior of Sidi Yahiya mosque is recognized by the yellow painted walls combined with the bottom of the walls, which consists of **unpainted bricks**. The mosque has a [courtyard](https://goo.gl/maps/Zsfd6eXb8iVWKYBU6), with walls made of bricks and a floor made of bright, square tiles.
clues.summary: Yellow-painted walls with an unpainted brick lower part. The courtyard has brick walls and bright square tiles on the floor.

clues.title: Road: rectangular tiles, brick houses
text: Coverage outside of the Djingareyber mosque in Timbuktu features brick buildings and a paved street with **rectangular** tiles.
clues.summary: Outside this mosque, brick buildings and a street paved with rectangular tiles.

clues.title: Mosque interior: round archways, red carpet
text: The inside of the Djingareyber mosque can be characterised by yellow painted walls, wide **round archways**, and red carpet.
clues.summary: Yellow painted walls, wide round archways and red carpet.

clues.title: Landmark: very sandy ground, pyramid tower
text: The Sankoré Mosque is surrounded by very **sandy** ground. The mosque itself has a prominent pyramid-shaped tower.
clues.summary: Very sandy ground around a mosque with a prominent pyramid-shaped tower.

clues.title: Landmark: richly decorated doors
text: The Sankoré Mosque has **richly decorated doors**, which are made of wood adorned with metal details.
clues.summary: Wooden doors decorated with metal details.

clues.title: Mosque interior: blue carpet, low ceiling
text: The interior of the Sankoré Mosque has blue carpet, yellow painted walls, and a **fairly low ceiling** supported by wooden beams.
clues.summary: Blue carpet, yellow walls and a fairly low ceiling held up by wooden beams.

clues.title: Landscape: empty reddish ground outside walls
text: The exterior of the mosque in Gao can be recognised by the **large desolate space** outside the walls, the ground consisting of reddish dirt, and some trees in the background.
clues.summary: A large empty space outside the mosque walls, reddish dirt ground, and a few trees in the distance.

clues.title: Mosque interior: low plain corridors
text: The inside of the Gao mosque consists of undecorated corridors with **low roofs**. You can see the **pyramid shaped structure**, with a very large number of dry branches sticking out of it, from the courtyard.
clues.summary: Undecorated corridors with low roofs. From the courtyard you see a pyramid-shaped structure with lots of dry branches sticking out.

clues.title: Landmark: mosque front, clear sky
text: The Djenné mosque has a very recognizable front, with some distant trees and a **clear sky**. The mosque is surrounded by low houses, making the area look fairly open.
clues.summary: A very recognisable mosque front with some distant trees and a clear sky. Low houses around it make the area look open.

clues.title: Mosque interior: dark, gothic arches
text: The interior of the Djenné mosque is quite dark, with a high roof and narrow corridors with **gothic arches**. There is also a large courtyard with sandy ground and brown wooden doors along the walls.
clues.summary: Quite dark inside, with a high roof, narrow corridors with gothic arches, and a big sandy courtyard with brown wooden doors along the walls.

clues.title: Landmark: similar mosque, closer trees
text: The Mopti mosque is similar in style to the Djenne mosque, but has **trees growing closer** to the walls and a slight amount of clouds in the sky. The streets with coverage around the walls of the mosque also appear more [narrow](https://goo.gl/maps/wYkmJf6fUAN6Fp2J7) than the ones in Djenne.
clues.summary: Similar in style to the previous mosque, but trees grow closer to the walls, there are a few clouds, and the streets around it look narrower.

clues.title: Mosque interior: open, blue carpet, no arches
text: The interior of the Mopti mosque can be recognised by the somewhat **open space,** with a high roof, no arches, and a blue carpet across the entire floor.
clues.summary: Open space with a high roof, no arches and blue carpet over the whole floor.

clues.title: Coverage: modern mosque, light blue walls
text: In the north west of Bamako, you can find a tripod inside an empty **modern mosque**. The interior’s light blue walls and pink floor make this location instantly recognizable.
The coverage on the exterior is in the mosque’s yard. The outside walls are made of concrete, and are painted yellow and orange.
This coverage is **severely misplaced**, being actually located in an unidentifiable rural area, rather than inside Bamako.
clues.summary: An empty modern mosque with light blue walls and a pink floor inside. Outside is a yard with yellow and orange concrete walls. The location is badly misplaced, actually in an unidentifiable rural area.

clues.title: Landscape: rocky gorge with dry trees
text: This natural **rocky gorge **is part of the [Bandiagara Escarpment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandiagara_Escarpment). It features dry trees and bushes following the path. It is located southwest of Sangha Ogol Leye, and is the only completely rural coverage in Mali.
clues.summary: A natural rocky gorge with dry trees and bushes along the path. It is the only fully rural coverage in the country.

clues.title: Coverage: misplaced shots inside a mosque
text: Inside the Sankore mosque coverage in Timbuktu (but not connected to it), there are **several misplaced locations**: The inside of a [tour business](https://goo.gl/maps/dqPgKDhM4aWPpLgb9) actually located in Bamako, [a classroom](https://www.google.com/maps/@16.7759426,-3.0056179,2a,90y,251.37h,85.19t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sc7XR-Xm-B-4AAAQ5TZIq-w!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu), a [couple](https://goo.gl/maps/9sbjs2gEbyaCahEw5) of [streets](https://goo.gl/maps/Su95KP4Ervi7Aeta9) and some [other](https://goo.gl/maps/x1Zn5UaRMGveqagMA) [miscellaneous](https://goo.gl/maps/86NpvddGG48R9PYn7) [places](https://goo.gl/maps/Gh7e3WcFX8eQCVTs5).
clues.summary: Several misplaced locations sit inside one mosque's coverage: a tour business office, a classroom, a couple of streets and other odd places.
